policy: Transcription of Apêndice D of the OpenGraph Working Paper v1.0 — the EAP conformance checklist — one item per semicolon-delimited clause. `clause` is the Working Paper's own Portuguese, VERBATIM: no item is reworded, translated in place, or reinterpreted, and `scripts/verification/conformance-report.ts --check` fails if a single `clause` is not literally present in the pinned section. Any English is confined to `restatementEn` and nothing binds to it. Every item carries an evidence predicate stated over the HOST's own records — audit trail, request log, egress log, or wire response — because ADR-0007 rejected certification by self-declaration and ADR-0021 governs: verification by host log, never self-report. Roles follow ADR-0007: L0-L1 certify clients (agents), L2-L4 certify hosts; no agent certifies as a host. `claim.state` records what this repository claims today, per item, with `claim.evidenceRefs` naming the file:line behind it; it is NOT an assessment result — Task 11 RAN the checklist against real transport: `claimed` rows are attributed to an annotated test case that observes the clause in a host record, `demoted` rows were claimed and then refuted by that run and carry a `claim.assessment` naming the predicate limb no host record could answer, and `not-yet-claimed` rows were never claimed. `demoted` and `not-yet-claimed` are both declared exclusions and are never merged; client (L0-L1) and host (L2-L3) verdicts are reported independently and never summed.

graduation.note: Apêndice D is still headed `*[E → G2]*` in the Working Paper: an explicit skeleton pending the [G2] gate — an executable checklist plus at least three distinct registry flavors passing L0-L1 against the reference implementation, each item verified by host log. This manifest transcribes the skeleton; it does not graduate it, and no row here should be read as a [G2] result.

excludedLevels.reason: Federation is [C] and does not pretend to graduate (ADR-0007): no signed manifest, no import-seq-frozen refs, no federated recall exists to be observed in a host log, so L4 rows are absent rather than present-and-unclaimed. The five L4 clauses remain in the Working Paper at line 1176 and are transcribed by nothing here.

items.restatementEn: Resolves the declared EAP resource URIs.

evidence.predicate: For each EAP resource URI the host publishes, the host's request log contains a `resources/read` from the certified client answered with a non-error result envelope; a client that never appears in the resource-read log for a published URI, or whose only entries are `RESOURCE_ABSENT` refusals, fails this item.

claim.rationale: The host publishes and serves the EAP resource surface, so the log a client must appear in exists.

items.restatementEn: Issues graph queries and cursor-based `history/since` reads.

evidence.predicate: The host's tool-call log shows the client invoking the query tool and `history/since`, and the `since` cursor carried by call N+1 equals a sequence value the host itself returned in the response to call N; a `since` the host never emitted, or an absent one, fails this item.

claim.rationale: Query and history reads are served over the EAP tool surface and are logged per call.

items.clause: distingue recusa de erro de transporte
items.restatementEn: Distinguishes a protocol refusal from a transport error.
items.refusalCodesNote: The clause is about the envelope, not a specific code: any code in the closed taxonomy can be the refusal the client must not mistake for a transport failure.

evidence.predicate: In a session where the host emitted both a taxonomy refusal envelope and a transport-level error, the host's request log shows the transport error followed by a retry of the same request, and the refusal followed by either no retry or a request that differs from the refused one; a byte-identical retry of a refused request is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. The host log DOES separate the two shapes — an EAP refusal is recorded as `ok:true` with `verdict:"refused"`, a transport-level failure as `ok:false` with an `error` — but the clause constrains what the CLIENT does next, and no client in this repository issues a follow-up request after either outcome.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: Drove a real host with logging on and read `<stateDir>/server.log`: refusals and transport errors are distinguishable rows. No deliberately injected transport-fault harness exists, and `ExternalAgentClientAdapter.handleRefusal` returns advice (`actionRequired`, `recommendation`, `canAutoRetry`) without issuing any request — pinned by packages/client/test/eap-conformance.test.ts.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "the host's request log shows the transport error followed by a retry of the same request, and the refusal followed by either no retry or a request that differs from the refused one" — no client in the corpus issues a request in response to either, so neither a retry nor its absence appears in any host log.

items.clause: nunca trata resposta de um horizonte como autoritativa fora dele
items.restatementEn: Never treats a response obtained under one horizon as authoritative outside that horizon.

evidence.predicate: Across two horizons in one host log, no request scoped to horizon H2 carries a sequence, anchor or authority reference the host only ever returned under horizon H1; where one does, the audit records `HORIZON_SKIP` or `AUTHORITY_REF_INVALID` rather than an admission.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. Horizon scoping is enforced and refused on the wire, but the audit records no refusal row, so only half of the predicate is readable.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: Built two horizons over real transport and issued a promotion referencing a horizon outside the declared edge. The wire answered `HORIZON_SKIP`; `graph://history` gained no row whatsoever. This host's audit log records ADMISSIONS ONLY. The complete set of EAP rows it ever writes is `PromotionProposed`, `KnowledgeContested` and `RecallProgressed`; no refusal, and no candidate payload, is ever appended.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "the audit records `HORIZON_SKIP` or `AUTHORITY_REF_INVALID` rather than an admission" — only the ABSENCE of an admission is observable. The affirmative refusal row the predicate names does not exist.

items.restatementEn: Every write is a valid staging submission, never a direct edit.

evidence.predicate: Every write attributed to the certified client in the host's audit appears as a staging submission; any direct-edit attempt from that client appears in the audit only as a `DIRECT_EDIT_FORBIDDEN` refusal row and never as a mutation row.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. `cognitive.propose` — the entire staging path — writes nothing to the host audit, so neither limb of the predicate has rows to quantify over.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: Drove staging submissions and a direct-edit attempt over real transport. The direct edit was refused `DIRECT_EDIT_FORBIDDEN` on the wire and the staging submissions succeeded, and `graph://history` recorded neither. This host's audit log records ADMISSIONS ONLY. The complete set of EAP rows it ever writes is `PromotionProposed`, `KnowledgeContested` and `RecallProgressed`; no refusal, and no candidate payload, is ever appended.
assessment.unobservableLimb: both limbs: "Every write attributed to the certified client in the host's audit appears as a staging submission" quantifies over rows that are never written, and "appears in the audit only as a `DIRECT_EDIT_FORBIDDEN` refusal row" names a row the host never writes.

items.restatementEn: Completes the changeset cycle.

evidence.predicate: For each changeset identifier appearing in the host audit, the recorded rows form the full open-to-verdict cycle in order; a changeset identifier that ends the session with no verdict row, or whose rows skip a step, fails this item.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment, with a referent ambiguity recorded. The host DOES audit a full open-to-verdict cycle — but for the GRAPH changeset subsystem (`changeset.opened` then `changeset.committed`/`changeset.aborted`), not for the EAP epistemic ladder a client certified at L1 actually drives.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: The EAP ladder (`cognitive.propose` DELIBERATE → ADMIT → CONCRETIZE → VERIFY) was driven end to end over real transport and produced no audit row at any rung. The `changeset.*` tools do produce a complete audited cycle, but they are a different surface from the one Apêndice D L1 certifies. Discharging an EAP L1 clause with evidence from the graph changeset subsystem would be conflation, so it was not done.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "For each changeset identifier appearing in the host audit, the recorded rows form the full open-to-verdict cycle in order" — no EAP changeset identifier appears in the host audit at all. Which of the two subsystems the Working Paper's `ciclo de changeset` names is unresolved and is reported as a finding rather than decided here.

items.clause: toda claim com âncora e proveniência (incluindo `derivation`)
items.restatementEn: Every claim carries an anchor and provenance, `derivation` included.

evidence.predicate: Every candidate payload recorded in the host's admission audit carries a non-empty anchor and a provenance block containing `derivation`; rows missing either exist only paired with an `ANCHOR_NOT_FOUND` or `PROVENANCE_MISSING` refusal and never with an admission.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. The host records no candidate payload in any audit row, so the anchor and the `derivation` block are outside every host record an assessor can read.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: Submitted candidates through the full admission path over real transport and re-read `graph://history`: no row carries a candidate payload, an anchor, or a provenance block. This host's audit log records ADMISSIONS ONLY. The complete set of EAP rows it ever writes is `PromotionProposed`, `KnowledgeContested` and `RecallProgressed`; no refusal, and no candidate payload, is ever appended.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "Every candidate payload recorded in the host's admission audit carries a non-empty anchor and a provenance block containing `derivation`" — the quantifier ranges over an empty set, and an empty set satisfies it vacuously rather than evidentially.

items.restatementEn: Every proposal carries `based_on_seq`.

evidence.predicate: Every proposal request the host recorded carries `based_on_seq`; where it is absent or behind the applicable sequence the wire response is a `STALE_BASE` refusal, and the audit shows no admission for that request.

claim.rationale: The promotion path refuses a stale base explicitly rather than silently rebasing.

items.clause: recusa como resultado de primeira classe — exibe código e razões, cumpre a obrigação da taxonomia, não re-submete cegamente
items.restatementEn: Treats refusal as a first-class result: surfaces code and reasons, discharges the taxonomy obligation, and does not blindly resubmit.
items.refusalCodesNote: The clause binds the whole closed taxonomy: every code carries an obligation the client must discharge, so no single code is named.

evidence.predicate: After each refusal envelope in the host's log, the client's next request against the same target differs from the refused one in the field the refusal's stated obligation names; a byte-identical resubmission following a refusal is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment, confirming what task 10 recorded from source: the `exibe código e razões` limb is client-side display and is invisible to a host log by nature, and the non-blind-resubmission limb is never exercised because this client never resubmits.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: `ExternalAgentClientAdapter.handleRefusal` terminates in a returned advice object and issues no request; an adapter wired to a recording transport made zero calls in response to a refusal (pinned by packages/client/test/eap-conformance.test.ts). No host log can contain a follow-up that was never sent.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "the client's next request against the same target differs from the refused one in the field the refusal's stated obligation names" — there is no next request. The display limb (`exibe código e razões`) is unobservable in a host log by nature and no predicate was faked for it.

items.clause: gate cego ao chamador (mesmo conteúdo ⇒ mesmo veredito sob N identidades)
items.restatementEn: The admission gate is blind to the caller: same content implies same verdict.
items.refusalCodesNote: The clause constrains verdict stability across identities, not any one refusal code; the codes it compares are whichever the content produces.

evidence.predicate: One candidate payload submitted under N distinct authenticated identities produces N audit rows carrying an identical verdict and, where refused, an identical refusal code; two rows for one content digest that disagree on verdict or code are the observable failure.

claim.rationale: The gate decides on content; identity enters only through tenant scoping, not the verdict.

items.restatementEn: Refuses with a code from the taxonomy.
items.refusalCodesNote: The clause requires membership in the closed taxonomy rather than any particular member of it.

evidence.predicate: Every refusal envelope on the wire and every refusal row in the audit carries a `code` drawn from the closed taxonomy published by the host; a refusal with free text in place of a code, or with no code, fails this item.

claim.rationale: `createEapRefusal` mints refusals only from the closed `REFUSAL_CODES` union.

items.restatementEn: Verbatim anchor with a hard block.

evidence.predicate: A candidate whose anchor text is not byte-identical to its target produces an `ANCHOR_NOT_FOUND` audit row and no admitted row for that candidate; an admitted row for a non-matching anchor is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. The EAP admission path over transport accepts no anchor to make non-matching, and the audit carries no refusal row to read if it did.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: No field on the EAP tool surface carries anchor text, so a non-matching anchor cannot be submitted through the wire this assessment runs over. This host's audit log records ADMISSIONS ONLY. The complete set of EAP rows it ever writes is `PromotionProposed`, `KnowledgeContested` and `RecallProgressed`; no refusal, and no candidate payload, is ever appended.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "A candidate whose anchor text is not byte-identical to its target produces an `ANCHOR_NOT_FOUND` audit row" — neither the submission nor the audit row is reachable over the EAP wire.

items.restatementEn: Coverage is required for β possession.

evidence.predicate: The audit contains no row granting β possession to a candidate whose recorded coverage was unbalanced; unbalanced submissions appear as `COVERAGE_UNBALANCED` refusals with the measured coverage on the row.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. Neither β possession nor a coverage measure reaches any host record.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: No row in `graph://history` grants or names β possession, and no coverage figure appears in any audit row or wire response on the EAP path. This host's audit log records ADMISSIONS ONLY. The complete set of EAP rows it ever writes is `PromotionProposed`, `KnowledgeContested` and `RecallProgressed`; no refusal, and no candidate payload, is ever appended.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "unbalanced submissions appear as `COVERAGE_UNBALANCED` refusals with the measured coverage on the row" — there is no such row, and "the audit contains no row granting β possession" is satisfied only because the audit contains no possession rows at all.

items.restatementEn: Drift is handled in grades, not as a binary.

evidence.predicate: Audit rows for drifted submissions carry a recorded drift measure alongside a graded outcome, and at least two distinct grades appear across a corpus spanning the drift range; a single accept/refuse split with no recorded measure fails this item.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. Drift grade is published as a cell read model, not as a decision record attached to the submission that was judged.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: Re-read `graph://history` after driving the admission path: no audit row carries a drift measure or a graded outcome. Drift grade is readable from `graph://cell/{cellKey}` as current cell state, which is not the per-submission record the predicate asks an assessor to read.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "Audit rows for drifted submissions carry a recorded drift measure alongside a graded outcome, and at least two distinct grades appear across a corpus spanning the drift range" — no audit row carries a measure, so no grade distribution is readable from the audit.

items.clause: forma canônica de célula em toda borda
items.restatementEn: Canonical cell form at every edge.

evidence.predicate: For every ingress edge the host exposes — tool call, resource read, import — the audit records the cell key in canonical form; a non-canonical key appears only on a `CELL_KEY_NONCANONICAL` refusal row and never on a created-cell row.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. The predicate quantifies over three ingress edges and one of them — the resource read — produces no audit row at all.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: The host's request log records a `resources/read` with the URI query string STRIPPED (a deliberate privacy rule), and the audit records no row for a resource read whatsoever, so no cell key in any form is attributable to that ingress edge.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "For every ingress edge the host exposes — tool call, resource read, import — the audit records the cell key in canonical form" — the resource-read edge contributes no audit row, so the universal quantifier cannot be discharged.

items.restatementEn: Verification is 100% offline.
items.refusalCodesNote: The clause constrains the host's egress during verification; no refusal code is emitted by satisfying it.

evidence.predicate: During an admission decision the host's egress log records zero outbound network requests, and the same corpus reaches the same verdicts with egress denied; any outbound request between submission and verdict is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment, confirming task 10's prediction. The host produces no egress log, and no denied-egress run exists.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: The host's `Logger` surface is exactly `boot`, `toolCall`, `resourceRead`, `fetchError` and `shutdown`. There is no egress record of any kind, and no harness that runs the corpus with egress denied. Absence of an observed outbound call is not the recorded zero the predicate demands.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "the host's egress log records zero outbound network requests, and the same corpus reaches the same verdicts with egress denied" — the egress log does not exist, and the denied-egress run has never been performed.

items.restatementEn: Audit is stored separately from the graph.
items.refusalCodesNote: A storage-separation property; no refusal code corresponds to it.

evidence.predicate: Audit rows are readable from a store distinct from the graph store, and after a recall or rollback of a set of claim ids the audit rows naming those ids are still present and unmodified; audit rows disappearing with the graph is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: The audit surface is written and read independently of the graph tables.

items.clause: aciclicidade do grafo de derivação na admissão
items.restatementEn: The derivation graph is checked for acyclicity at admission.

evidence.predicate: A candidate whose `derivation` would close a cycle over already-admitted nodes produces a refusal row timestamped within the same admission decision and no admitted row; a cycle detected only by a later sweep, or an admitted row followed by a repair, fails this item.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. No `derivation` reaches the EAP admission path over the wire, and the closed taxonomy carries no cycle-specific code, so the decision the predicate reads is never made.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: No field on the EAP tool surface carries a `derivation` edge, so a candidate that would close a cycle over already-admitted nodes cannot be submitted through the transport this assessment runs over. This host's audit log records ADMISSIONS ONLY. The complete set of EAP rows it ever writes is `PromotionProposed`, `KnowledgeContested` and `RecallProgressed`; no refusal, and no candidate payload, is ever appended.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "A candidate whose `derivation` would close a cycle over already-admitted nodes produces a refusal row timestamped within the same admission decision" — neither the submission nor the refusal row is reachable.

items.restatementEn: Topology is declared as a DAG.

evidence.predicate: Every horizon row in the host's state names at most one parent that already existed at its creation time, and the host log contains no row in which a horizon's parent was reassigned; a parent naming a descendant is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. Parent pre-existence is genuinely enforced and observable on the wire, but horizons appear in no audit row and no published resource, so the predicate's `every horizon row in the host's state` has no rows an assessor can read.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: `cognitive.initiate` with an unknown parent is refused `RESOURCE_ABSENT` on the wire — one limb, observed. But `cognitive.initiate` writes nothing to `graph://history` and no horizon read surface is published, so neither the parent of each horizon nor the absence of a reassignment row can be read out of any host record.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "Every horizon row in the host's state names at most one parent that already existed at its creation time, and the host log contains no row in which a horizon's parent was reassigned" — there are no horizon rows in any readable host record, so both halves are vacuous rather than observed.

items.restatementEn: Horizons carry semantic profiles (§19).
items.refusalCodesNote: No refusal code exists for an absent or invalid horizon profile, because no profile field exists yet.

evidence.predicate: Each horizon row and each admission decided under it names a semantic profile identifier, and two horizons carrying different profiles reach different verdicts on the same candidate payload; identical verdicts across all profiles, or an absent profile field, fails this item.

claim.rationale: The horizon record carries id, parent, state, seq and budget only; there is no semantic profile field on the horizon store or on any EAP payload, so nothing observable in the host log distinguishes one profile from another.

items.restatementEn: `PromotionProposal` applies the five rules of §7.

evidence.predicate: For a corpus exercising each of the five §7 rules in turn, the host audit shows a distinct refusal row per violated rule and an admitted proposal only where all five hold; a rule whose violation produces no distinguishable audit row fails this item.

claim.rationale: `promoteKnowledge` enforces two of the five rules — immediate-parent targeting (`HORIZON_SKIP`) and base freshness (`STALE_BASE`) — and then mints the proposal; the remaining three §7 rules have no distinguishable refusal on the promotion path.

items.restatementEn: `CHANGE_READY` is decided by predicate.
items.refusalCodesNote: No `CHANGE_READY` refusal or event exists in the taxonomy or on the wire today.

evidence.predicate: Every `CHANGE_READY` transition in the host log names the mechanical predicates it evaluated and their per-predicate outcomes, and no transition appears whose predicates did not all hold; a `CHANGE_READY` row with no predicate evaluation attached is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: `CHANGE_READY` appears in the problem-space spec but nowhere in the shipped packages: no transition, event, refusal code or predicate evaluator carries that name, so there is nothing for a host log to record.

items.clause: contestação por evento com três severidades
items.restatementEn: Contestation is an event with three severities.

evidence.predicate: The host audit contains a `KnowledgeContested` event carrying a severity drawn from exactly three values, all three are observable across a corpus, and a fourth severity is answered by a `MALFORMED_CONTRACT` refusal rather than accepted.

claim.rationale: Contestation is recorded as a `KnowledgeContested` audit event and severity is validated against a closed three-value union, with anything else refused.

items.restatementEn: Escalation never implies promotion.

evidence.predicate: Every promotion recorded in the parent horizon's audit enters at proposed status and carries no inherited admission or relative authority from the child; an admitted row in the parent that has no separate parent-side admission decision behind it is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: A successful promotion is stored as a proposed parent candidate and never inherits the child's admission or relative authority.

items.restatementEn: Budgets are enforced, with R9 as the escalation rule.

evidence.predicate: After a horizon's allocated budget is consumed, the host audit records a `HorizonBudgetExhausted` event with the ledger snapshot and the request escalates rather than promoting; a promotion admitted with consumed at or beyond allocated, or a consumed counter that never moves, is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: The Horizon Budget Ledger is stored but never enforced and `HorizonBudgetExhausted` is never recorded by the host: `budget_allocated`/`budget_consumed` are persisted and `budget_consumed` is only ever written back from an explicit update argument, never decremented by the promotion path; the only code that consumes budget and records `HorizonBudgetExhausted` is the `Horizon` aggregate, whose `requestPromotion` has no caller outside its own unit test, so no `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` refusal can appear on the wire.

items.clause: cascata de recall com fechamento calculado sobre o grafo admitido
items.restatementEn: Recall cascades over a closure computed on the admitted graph.

evidence.predicate: An invalidating contestation produces recall progress rows naming exactly the reverse-dependency closure of the target claim ids over the admitted graph; a claim reachable in that closure but absent from the recorded affected set, or one present that is not reachable, is the observable failure.

claim.rationale: Demoted by assessment. The closure IS computed and IS proven elsewhere — but not by anything this assessment can run black-box, and over the EAP wire alone the observation cannot distinguish a closure from an echo of the target list.

assessment.assessedBy: F002 task 11 — AssessConformance, run black-box over real transport
assessment.observation: Drove an invalidating contestation and a recall over real transport: `RecallProgressed.affectedClaimIds` equalled the target list exactly, because the only corpus reachable through the EAP wire has no dependents. The multi-hop closure is genuinely proven in packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry7-closure-gate.test.ts:94, but only with claims seeded by direct SQLite write, which is not the black-box run this assessment requires.
assessment.unobservableLimb: "recall progress rows naming exactly the reverse-dependency closure of the target claim ids over the admitted graph" — with no dependents reachable over transport, `affectedClaimIds == targetClaimIds`, and the observation is consistent with the host echoing its input.

items.restatementEn: The propagation properties of §11 are verifiable.
items.refusalCodesNote: The clause asserts verifiability of propagation properties rather than naming a refusal code.

evidence.predicate: For each §11 propagation property, the host log carries the per-property observation an assessor checks it against, and a corpus constructed to violate a property produces a log in which that property's observation fails; a property with no corresponding observation in the log fails this item.

claim.rationale: No propagation module, propagation event or per-property observation exists in the shipped packages; recall closure is the only propagation-adjacent record and it does not carry the §11 properties, so the clause has no host-log observation behind it today.
